title: Exact recall, refusal and repair
description: The Pleroma recovered 64 stored items exactly in 200 of 200 trials and refused all 12,800 reads past capacity.
claim: The exact key view recovered 64 items with no errors in 200 of 200 trials. Past capacity it refused every time and never answered wrongly. With 5 reserved keys any of 1 to 5 lost key harmonics was rebuilt, 300 of 300 times each, and one corrupted cell in either copy of a store was detected, 10,000 of 10,000 times.

method.workload: Checks of a keys-only store, the Pleroma's single-face special case. Exact recovery: store k distinct symbols from vocabularies of 4,096 and 2^20 symbols and read them back, at capacities from 1 to 96. Associative recall: store n key and value pairs from a codebook of 256 values and recall each value from its key. Repair and corruption: lost harmonics, one corrupted cell in either copy, and a lost store in a parity group, counted over the cases tried.
engines: Pleroma with reserved keys, a check prime and parity groups
method.verification: Every exact decode is re-encoded and must reproduce every stored element before it is returned. Each repair and corruption check counts the cases that matched a brute-force answer.
method.statistic: 200 trials per capacity point. Associative recall uses 20 random seeds, with a chance level of 0.39 percent. Repair and corruption checks are exhaustive or random within the stated count.
method.memory: Exact recovery is checked at about 2,064 and 2,580 bits of storage, and the recall table at 3,965 bits.
method.tie: The exact read in the recall table is decode then test, not a ShiftKeys read. It measures recall, not model quality.

losses: At 64 pairs the exact store is past its capacity and refuses every query, so it recalls none. It tells you it cannot answer instead of guessing.
limits: The exact store holds a number of entries proportional to the number of pairs and grows with context.
